references.text: The Lord warns against prophets who prophesy lies in his name: 'It is a lie, what they prophesy in my name' (Jer 14:14). Jesus similarly warns against those who come in his name and lead people astray.
'I have not sent these prophets, yet they run. I have not spoken to them, yet they prophesy' (Jer 23:21). False prophets who claim to bring God's message are a recurring theme that Jesus addresses.
Parallel text in Matthew's version of Jesus' end-times discourse: 'Watch out that no one leads you astray! For many will come in my name, saying, "I am the Messiah"' (Matt 24:4-5).
Parallel text in Mark's version of the end-times discourse: 'Watch out that no one leads you astray! Many will come in my name and say, "It is I." And they will lead many astray' (Mark 13:5-6).

Jesus repeats the warning against false messiahs and false prophets who perform great signs and wonders to lead even the elect astray: 'If anyone says to you then, "Look, here is the Messiah"... do not believe it' (Matt 24:23-26).
Paul urges: 'Let no one deceive you with empty words' (Eph 5:6). The warning against being led astray by deceivers reflects Jesus' warning in Luke 21:8.

Paul warns against being confused about the day of the Lord: 'Let no one deceive you in any way' (2 Thess 2:1-3). This parallels Jesus' warning that some will say, 'The time is near,' and deceive people.
John warns that 'many antichrists have appeared' (1 John 2:18). This fulfills Jesus' warning that many will come in his name and claim to be the Christ.

'Test the spirits to see whether they are from God, for many false prophets have gone out into the world' (1 John 4:1). The call to test the spirits is connected with Jesus' warning not to follow false messiahs.

Gamaliel mentions examples of Theudas and Judas the Galilean, who arose with messianic claims and gained followers, but both came to ruin (Acts 5:36-37). Concrete examples of those Jesus warned against.
